question.problem:
The function $f(x),$ defined as

$$
f(x)=\frac{k}{\sqrt{8x+3}}+2,\,x>-\frac{3}{8}
$$

has an inverse function given by 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{9}{2(x-2)^{2}}-\frac{3}{8},\,x>2.
$$

What is the value of $k?$ Assume that $k>0.$

$k=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{k}{\sqrt{8x+3}}+2
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{k}{\sqrt{8y+3}}+2.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{k}{\sqrt{8y+3}}+2 \\ x-2 & =\frac{k}{\sqrt{8y+3}} \\ \sqrt{8y+3} & =\frac{k}{x-2} \\ {(\sqrt{8y+3})}^{2} & ={(\frac{k}{x-2})}^{2} \\ 8y+3 & =\frac{{k}^{2}}{(x-2)^{2}} \\ 8y & =\frac{{k}^{2}}{(x-2)^{2}}-3 \\ y & =\frac{{k}^{2}}{8(x-2)^{2}}-\frac{3}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{{k}^{2}}{8(x-2)^{2}}-\frac{3}{8},\,x>2.
$$

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that

$$
\frac{{k}^{2}}{8}=\frac{9}{2}\,⟹\,k=6.
$$
